evidence.statement: Claims, answers, and explanations consistently match the supplied Azure source, including Foundry projects, model families, evaluation, deployment, and agents.
Each item presents one defensible answer or a clearly specified set/order of answers; distractors are separated by the scenario or source distinction.
Distractors usually represent nearby concepts or realistic task mismatches, such as GPT-5.x versus GPT-4.1 priorities and marketing versus support work.
Wrong-choice feedback explicitly diagnoses realistic confusions, including comparison tools versus project setup, chat models versus embeddings, and evaluators versus remediation.

The sequence begins with an applying item, then alternates across unrelated topics and returns to foundational definitions near the end; the generative-AI definition appears at item 15 and the model-versus-agent relationship at item 24.
The session uses multiple mechanics, but arrange-sentence items recur in close proximity and fill-blank items are also distributed as repeated recall checks.
Scenario stems and recall prompts vary, but four items use the same 'Arrange...' pattern and several fill-blank stems follow a similar direct-definition form.
Applied scenarios resemble credible product, support, education, legal, and software-development decisions and align with source use cases.
Incorrect-answer feedback generally explains the misconception, the consequence, and the source-aligned next step.
The session mixes foundational recall with applying and analyzing items, which is appropriate for checkpoint review, though the ordering does not steadily scaffold difficulty.
Key terms such as foundation model, model family, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.x, embedding model, evaluator, and Foundry project are used consistently with the source.

The artifact is accurate, varied, and well-feedbacked, but the exact sequence feels thematically discontinuous because foundational, use-case, model-selection, evaluation, and deployment items are interleaved without a clear instructional arc.
